task: Set up LastPass for accounting firm: add 3 logins, shared folder, Wi-Fi secure note, update accounting login password and move to another folder.

observations.what: The 'free' route (Personal free) actually starts a 30-day Premium trial; the first sign-up landed back on the login page and needed a second login with the same master password before the vault opened.
The add-password side panel needs only a name at first (URL/username/password required marks vary) and saved each login with a clear green success banner; three logins took about 7 actions each.
The first Add password form hid the Folder, Notes and Custom fields sections, which only appeared the second time I opened it, so folder assignment could not be set at creation for the first login.
The form layout shifts after validation errors (fields move down), so clicks aimed at old positions missed and had to be repeated.

Creating a shared folder in Sharing center opened an upgrade-to-Families modal even during the Premium trial, so a team shared folder for the accounting staff could not be made; I used a plain personal folder named Accounting Team instead.

After creating folders, the Passwords and Notes lists showed 'Accounting Team' as two separate empty headers, a display glitch that made the folder structure confusing, though the folder picker listed it once.
Adding the Wi-Fi secure note was quick: Notes page, plus button, name and free-text body, save; it appeared immediately as a tile.
The Change password button does not let you type a new password; it opens a how-to modal telling you to go to the site. You must instead overwrite the password field directly, which is not obvious.

Editing an item through the pencil icon on its tile, overwriting the password and picking a folder in the same panel, then Save moved it to the Accounting Team folder in one pass, with Username/Password history links available.
Grid and list toggle, sort by folder, and a Select/Actions bar on tiles make the vault easy to scan, but it has no bulk import hint for a 25-person firm beyond the extension prompt.
Typed a made-up email-style username that the harness refused, and an early Username entry did not register, costing extra steps.
